data: Attribution describes associations implied by one fitted shared PLS representation.
Feature, module, and pathway effects are not causal claims.
No p-values or significance decisions are produced; external orientation inference remains the caller's responsibility.
PLS-captured effects are a lossy inverse-transform view and are not a unique inverse of measured features.
Bootstrap stability is conditional on the fitted preprocessing contract and frozen PLS model.

The 'principal' component decomposes the tested angle estimand — principal-axis divergence between the groups' signed leading principal axes — while per-adjacent-transition contrasts describe where along the trajectory the group directions diverge; the two coincide only for two-stage designs. A degenerate principal contrast is reported with its flag and MUST NOT be read as a well-defined orientation.
